conclusion.contradictions: The five verdicts that exclude 10.0a -- 0x00043612 FUN_00043612 (4 bytes), 0x0004361a __CHK (12), 0x0004362a __GRO (3), 0x0004362d __STK (22), 0x0004364b __STKOVERFLOW (4) -- are all CLIB3S!stk386 and are an artifact, not a contradiction. WATCOM_10.0a\lib386\dos\clib3s.lib on this machine is 190,464 bytes with 393 modules and no stk386; 10.0a_infobase's is 190,976 with 394 and has it. Of the 393 shared modules zero differ by SHA-256, and EMU387/GRAPH/MATH387S/both STARTUP libs are identical module-for-module between the two installs. The sweep had nothing to compare against and the miss became an exclusion. Resolved by reading the two installs as one release; the damaged clib3s.lib should be replaced from the infobase install. With that resolved, no verdict fights the rest.
conclusion.summary: 395 verdicts, 381 informative (14 too short to compare), 392 high confidence. Raw intersection is the single label 10.0a_infobase; restricting to high-confidence verdicts gives the identical set. The split between 10.0a and 10.0a_infobase is entirely a damaged library file on this machine -- the WATCOM_10.0a install's clib3s.lib is missing the stk386 module (393 vs 394 modules, 190,464 vs 190,976 bytes), and all five verdicts excluding 10.0a are stk386 stubs; every other module in every library is SHA-identical between the two installs. Reading them as one release, the intersection is exactly one release: Watcom C/C++ 10.0a. 10.0 is excluded by 7 verdicts, led by __prtf at 0x0004c423 on 649 comparable bytes (606 mismatching against 10.0; 10.0's __prtf is 687 bytes with SUB ESP,0x48, the image's is 695 with SUB ESP,0x4c) and __isindst at 0x0005254b on 595 bytes, whose three timeutil siblings match 10.0 exactly at their offsets so the module was definitely parsed. 10.0b is excluded by only 2, but neither is thin: strtod at 0x00055443 on 443 comparable bytes with 362 mismatching, and IF@TAN at 0x00042ca0 which rests on just 5 bytes of its own yet is decided by a positional comparison of the entire 136-byte trig387 _TEXT segment against 10.0b's 152-byte version. 10.5+ is excluded by 105-111 verdicts and the 9.5 family by 270-272, so only the intra-family split needed care. Against the standing conclusion in rebuild_info/build_flags.md: the release agrees (10.0a), the caveat does not -- "10.0b not excludable, the two releases' relevant products are byte-identical" is superseded, since MATH387S's strtod and trig387 both changed at 10.0b and FDPS.LE carries the 10.0a form of both. The two short runs the standing conclusion cited (strupr, __CHP) are family-only evidence and never could have split 10.0a from 10.0b.
